ps140: 4, Podoben “As one valiant among the martyrs…”

Earnestly let us bless the glorious Bartholomew,* the never-setting star of the Sun of great splendour,* the animate heaven which proclaims the saving glory of God,* the divine preacher, the beacon of the nations,* the river which pours forth a stream of understanding* and waters the hearts of the faithful.

Your paths were revealed in the sea, O apostle,* and shown to be beyond the understanding of men;* for, cast into the sea in a casket,* you made your way to the West, O most renowned Bartholomew,* right glorious martyrs following you from the East on either side,* and rendering homage to you, at the behest of the Master of all.

With your wondrous ascents you purified the water,* and arrived at the island of Lipari,* pouring forth myrrh, O glorious one,* and healing incurable diseases;* and you became for the faithful in that place a saviour and refuge,* a deliverer and intercessor before the King and Saviour of all,* O Apostle Bartholomew.

Proclaiming the one Godhead in three Hypostases, you roiled the sea of polytheism,* and those drowning in the abyss of ungodliness you guided to calm havens, O blessed one.* Wherefore, you have received heavenly recompense,* entreating Him who loves mankind, in behalf of those who hymn you.

Having illumined your mind with divine radiance,* you travelled with the sun like a ray thereof, with Paul illumining the benighted, O godly Titus;* and with him you delivered the world from deepest night.* Wherefore, we call you blessed, as a God-pleasing hierarch,* a divine apostle and fervent intercessor.

Hailing from Crete and returning to there,* you established the true faith there as an unshakable foundation,* and edified the faithful there by the divine power of heaven, O blessed Titus,* first hierarch of your homeland, companion of Paul* and consolation of the faithful.

Forsaking earthly things, followed after Christ;* and having been marked by the inspiration of the Holy Spirit,* you were sent by Him to the nations who were perishing,* to turn the people to the light of the knowledge of God, O Apostle Bartholomew.* And having completed the divine feats of your suffering and undergone divers tortures,* you surrendered your soul to Christ, whom you entreat, O most blessed one,* that He grant us great mercy.
stavrotheotokion: She who knew not wedlock,* beholding You nailed to the tree of the Cross,* O Jesus, said weeping:* “O my sweet Child, why have You forsaken me* who alone gave You birth,* O unapproachable Light of the unoriginate Father?* Hasten and glorify Yourself,* so that those who glorify Your divine sufferings* may receive divine glory!”
